title: Gabriel
lead: Gabriel (the meaning of the name is debated: 'man of God' or 'God is my strength') is the angel who explains Daniel's visions (Daniel 8:16; 9:21), the first angel named in the Bible. In the New Testament he announces the births of John the Baptist and of Jesus (Luke 1:11-38). He is named in 1 Enoch among the chief angels, and in the Qur'an as Jibril.

sections.b: In Daniel 8:16 a voice over the Ulai calls, 'Gabriel, help this man understand what he saw.' He explains the ram and the goat. In 9:21 he comes in swift flight at the time of the evening offering and gives Daniel the seventy sevens. He appears as 'the man Gabriel' (9:21), as the figure in 8:15 who 'looked like a man' (gever, from the same root as his name), and may be the speaker of chapter 10 (the text does not say). He is not called an archangel in Daniel.

sections.h: Gabriel in the Gospel of Luke
sections.b: To Zechariah in the temple Gabriel says, "I am Gabriel, the one who stands before God" (Luke 1:19). To Mary in Nazareth the angel Gabriel announces the birth of Jesus (Luke 1:26-38). Luke's two scenes echo Daniel: Daniel's muteness in 10:15 and Zechariah's silence (Luke 1:20), and the timing of the evening offering in Daniel 9:21 and Luke 1:8-10 (the incense hour).
